app.title: VU3INI Climate Studio
app.tagline: Climate analysis for any place on Earth, from Google Earth Engine and your own weather station
notice.title: Personal-use notice
notice.must_accept: Please read and accept the notice to use the app.
connect.title: Connect Earth Engine
connect.intro: Analyses run on Google Earth Engine under your own free noncommercial Cloud project. Follow the steps, then paste your project ID.
connect.step1: Sign in with your Gmail account and open the registration page.
connect.step2: Click "Register a Noncommercial or Commercial Cloud Project", then choose "Unpaid usage".
connect.step3: Create a new Cloud project (or pick an existing one) and copy its project ID.
connect.step4: Answer the eligibility questions: personal learning, academic research or teaching.
connect.step5: Describe your work, click Register, then click Enable when asked to enable the API.
connect.step6: Return here, paste the project ID, click Sign in with Google, then Test connection.
connect.tips: Tips: do not add a billing account. Google may ask you to re-verify noncommercial use from time to time. Paid or client work needs a commercial registration instead.
connect.project_id_hint: 6–30 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter
status.not_configured: Earth Engine not set up yet
status.token_expired: Sign-in expired or missing. Click Sign in with Google.
status.not_registered: This project is not registered for Earth Engine, or the API is not enabled. See steps 2 and 5.
status.no_internet: No internet connection. Saved results and station data still work offline.
status.invalid_id: That is not a valid project ID: 6–30 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen.
area.title: Area
area.too_large: This area is very large ({km2:,.0f} km²). Processing may be slow or hit Earth Engine limits; consider a coarser scale.
area.boundary_note: Global boundary datasets may differ from official national boundaries. For official reports, upload the official boundary file.
period.title: Period
period.warn_trim: {dataset} starts on {start}; the period was trimmed to begin then.
period.warn_latest: Latest available {dataset} data: {date}. Results stop there.
period.warn_overlap: The baseline overlaps the analysis period. Anomalies are clearer when they are separate.
run.need_connection: Connect Earth Engine first (see Connect Earth Engine).

station.title: My Weather Station (Davis Vantage Pro2)
info.drought_vci.what: Compares how green the land is now with the greenest and brownest it has been in the same month in past years, on a 0–100 scale.
info.drought_vci.example: A VCI of 20 for Nagaon in March means crops are close to their worst March condition: a drought warning.
info.drought_temporal.what: Labels each month as no, mild, moderate, severe or extreme drought, showing when a drought starts, peaks and ends.
info.drought_temporal.example: Sonitpur might show "moderate" from February to April, then "none" once the monsoon arrives.
info.drought_modis.what: Combines greenness and land heat into one vegetation health score; brown and hot together means stronger drought.
info.drought_modis.example: Dry, unusually hot land in Karbi Anglong in April gets a low score before crops visibly fail.
info.heatwave_index.what: Counts runs of several days hotter than that place's usual hottest days, and their length and strength.
info.heatwave_index.example: Guwahati could show 3 heatwaves in a summer, the longest lasting 5 days.
info.heatwave_map.what: Draws a map of where heatwaves happened most often or most strongly.
info.heatwave_map.example: A district map showing which parts of Assam had the most heatwave days in a year.
info.temp_anomaly.what: Shows how much warmer or colder than normal a place or month was.
info.temp_anomaly.example: "+1.8 °C" for Jorhat in May means it was 1.8 °C warmer than an average May.
info.cold_spell.what: Counts runs of unusually cold days and how long they lasted.
info.cold_spell.example: Six cold nights in a row in Tawang in January count as one cold spell.
info.precip_forecast.what: Shows rain expected over the next few days from global forecast models.
info.precip_forecast.example: Before a field visit to Majuli, see that heavy rain is expected over the next three days.
info.precip_sdii.what: Average rain per rainy day; a rising value means rain is coming in heavier bursts.
info.precip_sdii.example: Dhemaji rising from 12 to 16 mm per rainy day means fewer but heavier downpours: more flash-flood risk.
info.precip_anomaly.what: Rainfall as a percentage of normal for that place and time.
info.precip_anomaly.example: June rain at 140% of normal in Lakhimpur points to flood risk; 60% points to a dry spell.
info.precip_cluster.what: Groups places or years that share a similar rainfall pattern.
info.precip_cluster.example: Splits Assam into zones such as "early heavy monsoon" and "late steady monsoon" to guide sowing.
info.precip_downscale.what: Turns a coarse rainfall map (about 5 km squares) into a finer one using terrain and vegetation.
info.precip_downscale.example: Shows rain differences between a valley floor and nearby hill slopes that a 5 km square hides.
info.lst_downscale.what: Sharpens 1 km land-surface temperature to about 30–100 m.
info.lst_downscale.example: Shows which Guwahati neighbourhoods are hottest, for urban heat planning.
info.era5_downscale.what: Sharpens coarse air temperature (about 9 km squares) to local scale.
info.era5_downscale.example: Estimates the temperature of one tea estate instead of a whole 9 km square.
info.snow_season.what: Finds the first and last snow-covered dates each winter and the season length.
info.snow_season.example: Shows whether Tawang's snow season got shorter between 2015 and 2025.
info.snow_melt.what: Tracks how quickly snow cover shrinks through spring.
info.snow_melt.example: Earlier, faster melt in the upper Brahmaputra catchment can mean river levels rise earlier.
info.climate_class.what: Divides an area into climate zones using temperature and rainfall.
info.climate_class.example: A map splitting North-East India into hot-humid plains, cool hills and cold high-altitude zones.
info.station_temperature.what: Daily highest, lowest and average temperature; hottest and coldest days; warm and cold nights.
info.station_rainfall.what: Daily and monthly rain totals, rain rate, longest wet and dry runs, heaviest one-hour and one-day rain.
info.station_rainfall.example: "July total 410 mm; 95 mm fell in a single day on 3 July."
info.station_wind.what: Wind rose (direction and speed), average speed, strongest gust and its time.
info.station_wind.example: "Winds mostly from the north-east; strongest gust 54 km/h during a storm."
info.station_humidity.what: Daily humidity and dew-point ranges, muggy hours, fog-risk nights.
info.station_humidity.example: "Dew point above 24 °C on 20 days: very muggy."
info.station_feelslike.what: Heat index and wind chill; hours in caution or danger bands.
info.station_pressure.what: Pressure trend and sudden drops that often come before storms.
info.station_pressure.example: "A 6 hPa drop in 12 hours before the 2 May storm."
info.station_solar.what: Sunshine energy per day, cloudy versus clear days, monthly totals.
info.station_solar.example: "Only 6 clear days in July; solar energy 40% lower than in April."
info.station_uv.what: Daily peak UV, hours in high and extreme bands, safe-outdoor-time guidance.
info.station_uv.example: "UV reached 11 (extreme) between 11 am and 1 pm on most May days."
info.station_soil.what: Soil water tension by depth, drying and wetting after rain, irrigation alerts.
info.station_soil.example: "Soil at 30 cm dried past the irrigation threshold after 10 rainless days."
info.station_et.what: Daily water lost from soil and plants, compared with rainfall (water balance).
info.station_et.example: "In March, plants lost 110 mm but rain gave only 40 mm: a 70 mm deficit."
info.station_validation.what: Station readings beside ERA5, CHIRPS and satellite soil moisture for the same spot and dates, with the difference.
info.station_validation.example: "Satellite under-estimated July rain at the campus by 18%."
info.station_summary.what: One-page climate summary: totals, averages, extremes, records broken.
info.prithvi_flood.what: An AI model (NASA–IBM Prithvi) finds flood water in satellite images, pixel by pixel.
info.prithvi_flood.example: A flood map for a Majuli block after a big rain, to compare with the radar flood map.
info.prithvi_landcover.what: An AI model (NASA–IBM Prithvi) labels land as crops, forest, water, settlements and so on.
info.prithvi_landcover.example: Shows which fields in a district are under crops this season.
examples.note: Example numbers are illustrations, not real results.
